comment: The vectors pinning Prima.RegistryRequest (cyfr-registry-request/v1) and Prima.HandleAnswer (cyfr-handle/v1), read by CYFR and by the registry at cyfr.run. Every side derives each public key from its seed; walks the identity entries to each head, reproducing its identifier, directory, key_epoch, recovery_epoch and live key; re-signs every request whose signer is named and reproduces its sig byte for byte, and its bytes as the JCS form of the request; verifies each verify case's bytes (the named request's JCS bytes, padded with trailing spaces to pad_with_spaces_to when present) as the registry named (its host and the directory every identity it accepts names) at now_ms (Unix milliseconds) under the named head, reaching the result or the refusal; does the same with each refusal's input (request, sent as its JSON, or raw, sent as those exact bytes; a request whose signer is null was altered after signing or is not signed at all); holds each handle and publisher spelling under slugs to the grammar of a handle.claim or publisher.claim body; and parses each answer's bytes for the handle and registry asked, reaching its result, which encodes back to those bytes, or its refusal. Refusals are checked in the order: size, JSON, exact keys and their types; protocol; registry; operation and body; expiry; the head's identifier; the head's directory; key_epoch; signature. A request expires at expires_at and may expire at most 360000 ms after the clock. JCS has no null, and a null anywhere is refused. Under codes, every refusal of the protocol and of the handle answer: CYFR's name, the code the registry writes in its error envelope {"errors":[{"code","message"}]} and the HTTP status; every refusal named under verify, refusals, envelopes and answers is one of them. Each envelope's bytes read back to the refusal named, or are refused as malformed_answer; an answer's bytes that are an envelope read back to its refusal. An envelope's first error carries a string message, and a null anywhere in an envelope is refused. A request is at most 16384 bytes as sent; one whose escaped content passes that bound is refused by its signer as by the registry.
